name: Stability Ball Dumbbell Bench Press
description: A dumbbell bench press performed while lying on a stability ball instead of a bench. The unstable surface requires the core, glutes, and lower body to work significantly harder to maintain a stable pressing position, turning a chest-focused exercise into a full-body stability challenge. The ball also allows greater shoulder range of motion than a standard bench.

execution.starting_position: Sit on a stability ball and walk forward until the ball is under the upper back and shoulders. Feet flat on the floor, hips extended, body forming a table-top position. Hold dumbbells at chest level.
execution.setup_instructions: Use a fully inflated stability ball appropriately sized for your height. Set up near a wall or rack to retrieve dumbbells safely. Keep feet wide for a more stable base.
steps: Step 1: Position with the ball under the upper back and shoulders, hips high, feet flat and wide. Hold dumbbells at chest level.
Step 2: Press the dumbbells upward to full arm extension above the chest.
Step 3: Lower the dumbbells under control back to the chest, maintaining hip height and ball position.
Step 4: Repeat. Focus on keeping the body table-top rigid throughout.
execution.breathing_instructions: Inhale at the bottom, exhale on the press.
common_mistakes: Hips dropping during the press — keep glutes contracted and hips high
Ball positioned too far down the back — it should support the upper back/shoulders
Using too heavy a weight, losing stability and control of the ball
safety_considerations: Have a spotter hand you the dumbbells once in position, or pick them up carefully by walking back along the ball
Ensure the ball is fully inflated — a soft ball compresses unpredictably
Use a non-slip surface under the ball
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full range from chest to full lockout. The ball allows the dumbbells to descend slightly past the chest level for a greater stretch.
coaching_cues: Squeeze your glutes to keep the hips up — a sag transfers load away from the chest
Keep feet wide and planted firmly — your base of support keeps the ball stable
